The proposed answer, 1 − 1/k, is wrong: it gives a threshold of 0 at k = 1, and the exponent in the derivation is off.

**Where the derivation fails.** The proposal claims P(p ≤ u) ~ u^{n/t}. Take a committee whose per-voter minimum scores m_v are small (as they must be for p to be small). The non-domination probability is p ≈ Σ over t-subsets of ∏ m_v. For p ≤ u, at most t−1 voters can have a non-small m_v. So at least n−t+1 voters need m_v ≲ u^{1/t}, and each such event has probability about k·u^{1/t}. This gives P(p ≤ u) ~ u^{(n−t+1)/t}, not u^{n/t}.

**Corrected threshold.** The expected number of α-dominating committees is then E[N_k] ~ m^{k − (n−t+1)/t}. It tends to ∞ when k > (n+1)/t − 1 and to 0 when k < (n+1)/t − 1. With t ~ n(1−α) and n large, the condition becomes k + 1 > 1/(1−α). So the threshold is α* = 1 − 1/(k+1) = k/(k+1).

**Sanity check at k = 1.** The corrected formula gives 1/2, which is plausible for a single dominating candidate. The proposal's 1 − 1/k gives 0, which is not.

VERDICT: REJECT
